experiments.name: base operand path

latencies.notes: Latency from the base operand rj to the destination. The bound operand is held at 0x7fffffffffffffff so the range check always passes; the loaded value is turned back into an address with add.d, whose cycle is subtracted.

experiments.name: bound operand path

latencies.notes: Latency from the bound operand rk to the destination. The instruction loads when rj <= rk, so the loaded value cannot be used as the next bound directly (it would fail the check); it is added back to the base with add.d, whose cycle is subtracted. The 4-cycle direct form that ldgt.* shows is therefore not constructible for ldle.*; the fifth cycle is the added ALU operation.

throughput.name: 8 independent addresses
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r21, $r20, 0; addi.d $r23, $r20, 8; addi.d $r24, $r20, 16; addi.d $r25, $r20, 24; addi.d $r26, $r20, 32; addi.d $r27, $r20, 40; addi.d $r28, $r20, 48; addi.d $r29, $r20, 56; addi.d $r30, $r20, 1024; addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8' --asm 'ldle.b $r12, $r21, $r30; ldle.b $r13, $r23, $r30; ldle.b $r14, $r24, $r30; ldle.b $r15, $r25, $r30; ldle.b $r16, $r26, $r30; ldle.b $r17, $r27, $r30; ldle.b $r18, $r28, $r30; ldle.b $r19, $r29, $r30'
throughput.notes: 8 independent lanes: 7.98 core cycles per 8 instructions, CPI 1. Slope method (--unroll 1000, --unroll2 2000).

notes: Latency measured per source operand on LA464: base operand rj -> destination 5 cycles, bound operand rk -> destination 5 cycles. The instruction loads when rj <= rk and raises a bounds-check exception when the check fails, so every chain keeps the check passing. The 64-byte-aligned buffer holds 8 and 0 so the chase stays inside one cache line.
